correctness.rationale: With a universal center, a zero center is impossible (no vertex at distance two), and distance two between peripheral vertices means different clique petals. Every valid function has positive center and nonisolated positive support. Sorting by zero, one, or at least two petals containing label two gives an exhaustive disjoint polynomial decomposition, with exact minimum weights M+1, s_i+2, and five respectively. The counting of minima and the contiguous full weight spectrum follow from that classification and validity-preserving unit label increments. A direct independent shortest-path exhaustive verifier matched all polynomial coefficients on ten profiles, 1,881,792 ternary labelings total, largest order thirteen. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The documented 2023 foundational work gives the hop-total-Roman definition, paths/cycles and small-weight characterizations, but the indexed material inspected does not state a full labeled weight census of heterogeneous clique bouquets. A full public proof of the ordinary total Roman polynomial on the identical bouquet family uses adjacency defenders instead of exact distance-two defenders and gives a different minimum; the full hop-total-Roman matching-deleted biclique proof uses the same predicate on nonisomorphic graphs with distance-two neighborhoods inside shores; the full total two-rainbow bouquet proof uses a different label alphabet and different defense rule. These do not imply the present formula, its optimizer counts, or its all-weight interval. Published research records and literature queries yielded no identified equivalent or dominating result. This is best-knowledge and provisional, not a guarantee of priority.
residual_risks: The publisher full text of the 2023 foundational article was not completely accessible, despite indexed excerpts; a more specific result in uninspected sections remains possible.
Unindexed preprints, tables or semantically equivalent weight-enumerator results could predate this finding; database non-matches are not proof of uniqueness.
The general 2023 weight-four criterion may imply the minimum-four subfamily; originality relies on the full polynomial and all-parameter optimizer count, not the scalar branch.

value.rationale: The complete labeled hop-total-Roman weight polynomial for every heterogeneous clique bouquet is a natural infinite-family graph invariant, not a parameter-chosen computation. Distinct geometric defense strategies generate the size-two transition from weight five to four and an exact 3r_3 correction in minimum multiplicity; a separate monotonicity argument proves all integer weights up to 2(M+1) occur. These exact structural and counting properties are not entailed by an existing scalar small-weight bound, and give a reusable benchmark for hop-defense enumeration under clique-size heterogeneity.
